title: The Banner of Hidden Colors
markdown:
The annual Sunbeam Festival was a peaceful affair in Willow Creek: a day to welcome the longest, warmest day of the year. The square shimmered with gentle lights, a lovely hello to the sunshine. Leah the builder, pockets full of interesting little treasures, and Milo the mole, who loved the festival from his underground cozy spot, were especially looking forward to it. Professor Calder, whose laboratory was a quiet wonderland of lenses and light, had helped make a brand-new banner, promising a special sight.

When the banner unfurled high above the square, a quiet sigh floated through the townsfolk. It looked a little plain. Golden suns that should have gleamed were a dull pale yellow. Sky blues like cloudy greys. Cheerful reds a muted blush.

“Oh dear,” Leah murmured, tilting her head. “It’s supposed to be so bright.”

Milo peeked from the edge of the stage, whiskers twitching. “It forgot to bring its sparkle,” he whispered to a dandelion.

Calder, who usually beamed at a reveal, frowned at his neatly trimmed chin. “It doesn’t seem to be sharing all its colours today.”

The banner hung in the shade of the meeting hall, where the light was yellowish and thin.

Later, in Calder’s laboratory, golden sun streamed through the tall arched window and played on dusty shelves. A thought flickered.

“Leah, Milo, do come here. Please come near. I think we’ve been looking at this light all wrong.”

He picked up a smooth clear prism. “This white light from the sun? A secret party of colours, all mixed, hiding inside.” He tilted the glass. A breathtaking arc — red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet — danced across the far wall.

“Wow,” Leah breathed. “A real rainbow.”

Milo forgot his burrow. “Gentle magic!”

“Not magic. How the world works.” Calder rummaged and drew thin coloured sheets, translucent jewels. “Filters. Polite gates for colours. They decide who may pass.” He held a red filter over a scrap of banner. The blue bits went dark, almost black: the red gate had asked blue to wait. The yellow sun turned warmer, odd, not quite itself.

Leah’s builder-mind lit. “So if the banner looks dull, maybe we’re not giving it the whole party. Maybe the colours are there, and the light is hiding them.”

A secret party of colours, waiting.

They hurried back to the square, not to paste filters on the cloth, but to do something simpler. Leah and Milo, with Calder’s nod, moved the banner out of the hall’s shade into the full, honest sun of the longest day. White light — the whole generous blend — fell on the dyes. Dull greys bloomed toward true blue. Muted reds found their warmth. The pale yellow suns remembered gold.

Calder beamed, quiet joy. “White light is all the rainbow dancing together. The dyes were always there. They needed the whole party, not a shady leftover.”

Leah and Milo looked up at the reawakened banner, then at each other. The festival was ready to shine. As the last glow faded and stars began to pepper the velvet sky, they felt a comfortable weariness. The world was quiet, full of soft colours and gentle dreams. Milo yawned all the way to his burrow. Leah emptied her pockets of prism-shine and dandelion fluff, and wondered what other plain things were secretly throwing a party, if you only let the sun in.
characters: Leah (an observant builder), Milo (a mole), Calder (a professor)
author: StoryGen Community
